headline: Analyses a perceived rise in ASX company requests for shareholder approval of executive termination benefits during the 2025 AGM season.
reasoning: Longwave observed an apparent increase in companies seeking separate shareholder approval resolutions for executive termination benefits during the most recent AGM season, prompting a detailed review of their portfolio holdings over the last five years. After analysing AGM Notice of Meeting data across 114–127 portfolio stocks, they found 88 mentioned termination benefits or related legislative provisions. The piece contextualises this within Australia's long regulatory history of governing termination payments, from the seven-times threshold pre-2009 to the current one-year base salary threshold introduced by the 2009 Corporations Amendment Act, noting that 15 years of 'executive pay creep' since the last major reform may be quietly eroding the spirit of shareholder oversight.
